title: Stability playbook prioritization with Valencia Health
summary: Follow-up bridge call after the September 30 long-tail latency regression. Reviewed root causes, short-term mitigations, prioritized stability playbook items, and agreed next steps for runbook updates, targeted benchmarks in the dedicated pool, and an SLO proposal for token-level latency. Customer emphasized data residency and audit log requirements for any retained traces.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-14
- Start time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 51 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Kai Ortiz (CSM) — Priya Kumar (CTO), Samir Iqbal (VP Eng), Lena Morales (SRE)

Summary: Quick recap, then deep dive into artifacts, then playbook prioritization, then action items.

[00:00:05] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on fairly short notice. We wanted to run through the notes from the 9/30 regression and propose a stability playbook to prevent repeats. Kai, Maya and I will share updates.

[00:00:22] Priya Kumar: Thanks Jordan. Appreciate the triage work. Our legal team is still asking about retention of user prompts in logs so we'll need clear statements on what is stored and for how long.

[00:00:35] Kai Ortiz: Noted, Priya. We have a security section later; we'll make sure to call out audit log TTL and KMS usage.

[00:00:48] Maya Chen: Quick technical recap — on 9/30 we saw sustained tail latency spikes starting around 02:10 UTC after a deploy. The dedicated pool with mixed-model routing started queuing up large batched requests, and we hit an OOM on one host which caused several pods to restart. There was a fallback to a smaller model but the routing policy didn't kick over fast enough so some requests sat in queue — long tail.

[00:01:15] Samir Iqbal: Right, and that resulted in a bunch of 504s for our internal API. We lost transaction context and had to manually reconcile about 40 sessions.

[00:01:26] Lena Morales: Our metrics show a sudden widening in request size distribution — maybe a change in prompt template caused longer sequences. We also saw KV cash misses — the transcriber had it as KV cash earlier, ha — but the cache TTL was low after the deploy and warm-up was slow.

[00:01:45] Jordan Patel: Yeah small transcription errors aside, that's useful. Maya, do we have a clear root cause?

[00:01:52] Maya Chen: The short version: two things aligned. One, a prompt template change that increased average token length by ~30-40% for a subset of traffic. Two, the autoscaling policy was tuned for median latency and not for tail, so batch size grew under perceived throughput. The larger batches exceeded memory on certain GPU types under that model + quantization combo. The runtime should have prevented oversize batches but the kernel selection path for that particular model variant fell back to a slower execution path — we have a hypothesis that the mixed kernel fallback increased latency which fed into the batching feedback loop.

[00:02:30] Priya Kumar: So it's a combination of prompt drift and autoscaler policy mismatch. Anything about network or VPC peering? We didn't see congestion in the VPC.

[00:02:39] Maya Chen: No, network looked fine. There was one anomalous spike in peering latency but not enough to cause the cascade. The cascade was mostly internal to the serving runtime.

[00:02:51] Samir Iqbal: We'd like to avoid future sessions where we have to do manual reconciliation. What's staged as a short term fix?

[00:02:58] Jordan Patel: Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) Increase prefix/KV cache TTL and proactively warm caches for the affected route during peak hours. 2) Add a fast fallback policy that routes to a smaller, lower-memory model within 2 seconds of latency SLO breach. 3) Temporarily lower max batch size for that route until we complete kernel selection fixes.

[00:03:20] Lena Morales: Lowering max batch size is probably the quickest. Can we do that without redeploying?

[00:03:26] Maya Chen: Yes — configurable in the route policy. We can push a change to the route config and it will take effect at the next cycle. We'll send the change and monitor.

[00:03:36] Kai Ortiz: Also we recommended a fixed canary window for deploys to that route — basically hold scale and routing steady for 15 minutes post-deploy while we watch metrics.

[00:03:46] Priya Kumar: That sounds reasonable. On the security side, if you adjust cache TTLs and warm caches, what are the implications for PII?

[00:03:55] Jordan Patel: We don't store raw customer inputs in persistent logs by default. Cache entries are ephemeral and can be configured to avoid storing user identifiers. We'll share the cache-policy doc.

[00:04:07] Samir Iqbal: Can we get exact SLO thresholds? We currently have an internal 95th of 350ms for interactive calls. We need a token-level metric for the service.

[00:04:17] Maya Chen: We'll propose a draft SLO: 95th token latency under 450ms for the affected route, with an error budget aligned to your current 350ms at 90th. That gives breathing room for model variance. We'll share a spreadsheet mapping traffic to SLO buckets.

[00:04:33] Priya Kumar: Sounds good.

[00:04:38] Jordan Patel: Let's walk through evidence. Maya, you had some traces?

[00:04:41] Maya Chen: Yes, I uploaded three flamegraphs and two trace samples to the shared folder (link in chat). In trace A you can see the kernel selection path taking an extra 180ms due to fallback. Trace B shows batch accumulation over 600ms before dispatch.

[00:04:58] Lena Morales: Those traces line up with what we saw. Do you have model version pinned information? We want to pin a safe model until kernel fixes land.

[00:05:06] Maya Chen: We recommend pinning to model v2.3-stable for the next two weeks for that tenant. It's slightly larger but has a more stable kernel path. We'll provide a checklist to roll back to v2.3-stable via your console.

[00:05:18] Samir Iqbal: How about dedicated pool sizing? Several of our hosts are G5-ish and one node failed; is it a machine-level mismatch?

[00:05:25] Maya Chen: The failure happened on a host with mixed load and older GPU kernels. We're proposing a targeted capacity refresh: mark oldest host class as no-new-alloc and drain over next maintenance window. We'll coordinate times.

[00:05:36] Priya Kumar: Maintenance window needs to be after 02:00 UTC to avoid our US East mornings.

[00:05:41] Jordan Patel: Noted.

[00:05:44] Lena Morales: On observability, we want token-level latency logs and a breakdown by model variant. Right now our dashboard shows only route-level p50/p95.

[00:05:53] Kai Ortiz: We can add token-level histograms for the route. It will be an extra retention cost though — we'll estimate and include that in the proposal.

[00:06:01] Samir Iqbal: We'll pay for it if it prevents manual work.

[00:06:04] Priya Kumar: One more ask — can we get an audit trail of who triggered the fallback and model pin changes, for compliance?

[00:06:11] Jordan Patel: Yes, operator actions are logged. We can export the audit events and include them in the runbook.

[00:06:16] Maya Chen: Moving to prioritization — we suggested a 1–3 week timeline for short-term items: lower max batch and push fast fallback (within 48 hours), pin model (within 72 hours), warm caches and increase TTLs (within 1 week), schedule capacity refresh (2–3 weeks). Long-term items include kernel selection fixes, autoscaler changes to be tail-aware, and improved pre-deploy canary tooling.

[00:06:42] Samir Iqbal: That's a lot. Can we sequence them? We want smallest blast radius first.

[00:06:47] Maya Chen: Sequence proposed: 1) Route config change to lower max batch (48h), 2) Fast fallback policy (48h), 3) Model pin (72h), 4) Cache warm/TTL (1 week), 5) Observability token histograms (1 week), 6) Capacity refresh (2–3 weeks), 7) Kernel fixes (Q4 engineering slot).

[00:07:10] Priya Kumar: For the fallback policy, what happens to accuracy? We care about hallucination rates for clinical prompts.

[00:07:17] Maya Chen: The fallback model is calibrated for lower memory and slightly smaller context; we'll add a guardrail to avoid switching for prompts that require full context. We can also add post-response validation for clinical keywords as an added safety check.

[00:07:31] Lena Morales: We need to keep an audit trail of any fallback-triggered responses for a month for incident review.

[00:07:38] Jordan Patel: We can store those in a redacted trace bucket with PII removed. We'll document the redaction rules.

[00:07:44] Samir Iqbal: On the kernel selection fix, what's the ETA?

[00:07:48] Maya Chen: Engineering has a Q4 slot — early November to land a patch. We will provide interim mitigations in the rollout until the patch is in.

[00:07:58] Priya Kumar: Will that require any agent updates on our side?

[00:08:01] Maya Chen: No agent changes, it's runtime side. We'll handle compatibility.

[00:08:06] Jordan Patel: Let's capture open questions — Priya asked about PII retention on caches, Samir asked for SLO numbers, Lena asked for token histograms and traces for 9/30, we owe the exact maintenance window options, and Maya owes the model pin checklist.

[00:08:24] Kai Ortiz: I'll summarize in the CRM and create a task list.

[00:08:29] Priya Kumar: Also: can you provide a post-incident email doc that our execs can read? High level, impact, mitigation, next steps.

[00:08:38] Jordan Patel: Yes — we'll draft a short executive summary and email template.

[00:08:45] Samir Iqbal: For the capacity refresh, we want a non-disruptive drain plan. Please include stretchers for fallback if drain takes longer than planned.

[00:08:56] Maya Chen: We'll include an automated drain with health checks and a manual abort button.

[00:09:01] Lena Morales: Anything on cost? If we increase token-level logging and retention we want an estimate.

[00:09:06] Kai Ortiz: We'll include both increased infra cost and monitoring costs in the proposal.

[00:09:10] Priya Kumar: Are there any competitors we should be thinking about if we need feature parity for compliance?

[00:09:15] Jordan Patel: Competitors mentioned in prior conversations: Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, and OpenAI managed endpoints. We'll include a short comparison on audit features.

[00:09:25] Samir Iqbal: Ok. Let's do next steps and owners.

[00:09:28] Jordan Patel: I'll read them out.

Action items (as discussed):
- Jordan Patel: Draft exec email + post-incident summary and share with Priya by 2026-10-16.
- Maya Chen: Push route config change to lower max batch for the affected route and add fast fallback policy; target 48 hours (by 2026-10-16) and send runbook.
- Maya Chen: Provide model pin checklist and steps to set v2.3-stable; target 72 hours (by 2026-10-17).
- Kai Ortiz: Estimate cost impact for token-level histograms and retention; deliver estimate by 2026-10-19.
- Valencia Health (Samir/Lena): Share internal prompt-template diffs for the affected route so we can validate prompt drift; target 2026-10-15.
- Jordan Patel/Kai Ortiz: Propose two maintenance windows for capacity refresh (after 02:00 UTC) by 2026-10-18.
- Redwood Eng (Maya contact): Provide timeline for kernel selection patch & interim mitigations (by 2026-10-20).

[00:12:05] Priya Kumar: That reads well. Will you include a simple rollback play and checkpoints?

[00:12:11] Jordan Patel: Yes. We'll include a rollback checklist that includes immediate route pin and traffic cutover to hosted fallback in worst case.

[00:12:18] Samir Iqbal: We want a final postmortem once kernel fix lands.

[00:12:21] Maya Chen: Absolutely — we'll coordinate a final RCA call after patch.

[00:12:26] Lena Morales: Thanks everyone. One last ask: can we have a shared Slack channel for incident follow-up with Redwood engineers? That will speed up communication.

[00:12:33] Kai Ortiz: We'll set up a channel with limited retention and link it in the notes.

[00:12:38] Jordan Patel: Great. If nothing else, we'll close the call. Thanks all, expect the email and runbook updates soon.

[00:12:46] Priya Kumar: Thanks. Bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: This is an imperfect automated transcript. A few technical terms and proper nouns may be misrecognized (e.g., KV cash vs KV cache). Timestamps are approximate.
